subject: physics
title: Kinetic Theory and Internal Energy
welcome_lead: Connect microscopic motion to macroscopic temperature with ½ m c² = 3/2 kT.
meta_desc: A-Level Thermal Physics adventure on kinetic theory linking T to particle KE.
final_note: Temperature is just the mean kinetic energy of particles in disguise.

concepts.def: Model treating gas as fast-moving particles.
Average of v² across all particles.
½ m c² = 3/2 kT per molecule.
Sum of KE + PE of all particles.
U = 3/2 N k T (only translational KE).

walkthroughs.body_html: Pressure arises from molecular impacts. Result: pV = ⅓ N m c² where c² is mean square speed. Combine with pV = NkT to get ½ m c² = 3/2 kT.
Mean translational KE per molecule = 3/2 kT. Higher T = faster particles. At T = 0 K, motion stops (classically).
For ideal monatomic gas, all internal energy is translational KE: U = N × 3/2 kT = 3/2 nRT. Real molecules also have rotational and vibrational modes.
